signature: _generic_func_info(name: str, start0: int, end0: int, source_lines: list[str], lang_cfg: dict) -> dict
pre_condition: name is a non-empty string. start0 and end0 are integers satisfying 0 ≤ start0 ≤ end0 < len(source_lines). source_lines is a non-empty list of strings with trailing carriage-return and newline characters stripped. lang_cfg is a dict containing at least a 'keywords' key whose value is a set of strings.
post_condition: Returns a dict with exactly eight keys: 'name', 'start', 'end', 'calls', 'idents', 'body_words', 'exc_types', 'docstring'. 'name' equals the input name string unchanged. 'start' equals start0 + 1 (1-based start line). 'end' equals end0 + 1 (1-based end line). 'calls' is a set of strings where each string is a call-like identifier token occurring in the text formed by joining source_lines[start0:end0+1] with newline separators, excluding any token that is a case-sensitive exact member of lang_cfg['keywords']. 'idents' is a set of lowercase identifier-like tokens from the same body text. 'body_words' is a set of lowercase alphabetic tokens of four or more ASCII letters from the same body text, excluding English stop words. 'exc_types' is a set of lowercase exception-type-name tokens from the same body text. 'docstring' is the empty string. All set-valued entries are Python set objects, possibly empty; the keys are never absent. The function does not raise an exception, even when the body text is empty or contains no tokens matching any extraction pattern.
